key_insight: A physics-constrained, data-driven turbulence model can be trained at low Reynolds number and extrapolated to much higher Reynolds numbers while keeping formal computational cost near O(log(Re)) under stated assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical route to more accurate wall-bounded flow predictions without the prohibitive cost growth usually associated with high-Reynolds-number turbulence simulations.
method: Augment the Spalart–Allmaras RANS model using field inversion and machine learning.
Impose a constrained formulation that preserves the law of the wall and other physics behavior.
Train on affordable low-Re high-fidelity data, then deploy the model at higher Re for extrapolation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful transfer from channel flow trained at Re_tau=1000 to Re_tau=5200, and from periodic hill training at Re_b=5600 to tests at Re_b=10595, 19000, and 37000, with the constrained model giving the lowest RMSE and nearly Re-independent error.
watch_item: The favorable O(log(Re)) cost claim depends on assumptions such as mean-flow-aligned grids, fixed spanwise resolution, and steady-solver linear cost, so performance may change outside those conditions.
paper_title: A formal log(Re)-cost framework for the engineering turbulence problem
